acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The state machine is closed: every state has an explicit set of allowed transitions and causers; no transition leads out of OUTCOME_UNKNOWN except a reconciliation record or an authorised intervention.

AC-2: The crash matrix (§8) covers all five crash points and, for each, names the resulting state, whether a second device contact is possible (must be 'no' for any point after contact), and what the operator sees.
AC-3: Lease/heartbeat/fencing rules make it impossible for two workers to execute the same step attempt; the mechanism is specific enough for a Testcontainers test.
AC-4: Retry rules are stated per action class of utils/action_taxonomy.py; operational-write never auto-retries.
AC-5: Owner, approver(s) and execution identity are three distinct fields with their sources; the scheduled-job actor problem from the brief (SR-D6) is resolved.
AC-6: Pre-execution checks are enumerated in order with their recorded outcome fields and run before any device contact.
AC-7: Run Now is specified as a job request satisfying UI-OPERATIONAL-RUN-NOW and APPROVAL-MODEL, with the approval state checked at claim time, not only at request time.
AC-8: Schedule optimistic concurrency refuses on version conflict; the refusal shape is defined.
AC-9: §9 provides at least ten testable acceptance criteria for B1-4 / B1-10 / B1-11.
AC-10: §10 lists every contradiction with frozen authority found (or states none and which documents were checked); the document reopens no PO-reserved decision.

context_not_loaded: Any Java source, Gradle build or Flyway migration -- B1-4 implements this contract
Line-1 execution paths (utils/collection_executor.py::workflow_argv, console/runner.py::_execute, main.py) as anything other than reference: the Java worker never invokes them (workflow P-1)
The backup profile rules themselves (C7) and the capability/step definitions (C4) beyond the minimal step interface named above
invariants: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is a terminal-until-reconciled state: a job whose write was sent but whose result could not be recorded never auto-retries a write; reopening requires a reconciliation record (what evidence, who) or a separately authorised intervention -- exactly acceptance sentence A-2
Read-class steps may be retried under explicit, bounded rules; operational-write steps never auto-retry; the contract states the rule per action class of utils/action_taxonomy.py

Exactly-once device contact per step attempt is proven by design: lease ownership + fencing token + step-attempt record written BEFORE the device is contacted; the crash scenario (worker dies after sending the command, before recording the result) must land in OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no second contact -- B1-11 will test this

Owner (who created the request/schedule), approver(s) (who approved the profile version / schedule / per-operation approval) and execution identity (which credential reference the worker used) are three distinct recorded fields; 'last editor' is never the execution identity

Pre-execution checks (E1-E7 gate chain, D7 role, approval state of profile version + target + schedule, connectivity check where required, Line-1/Java contact-coordination window per workflow §3.4) run at claim time, before any device contact, and their result is recorded on the job
Class-1 actions remain non-submittable from a console; a Run Now is a job request, never a console submission (UI-OPERATIONAL-RUN-NOW)
Schedule edits use optimistic concurrency (version check) and refuse on conflict; they never clamp or silently merge (design §6.7 semantics preserved)
No decision frozen in UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md is reopened; contradictions with frozen authority are REPORTED in a dedicated section
